lines: Turns one 1V/oct pitch into a four-note chord, with a list of stored chords stepped by trigger or picked by voltage
The note this output carries, dragged round the chromatic circle and shown in volts; a full 360° turn moves it an octave
Drag to transpose every note of the chord in semitones
The voltage here shifts all four outputs, and the chromatic circle is relettered so its top note is the root
A trigger here sets the chord number back to 1
A trigger here steps to the next chord and wraps round to 1 after the last one
0V to 10V picks a chord directly, the range divided evenly between the chords stored, and voltages outside it wrap round. A cable here overrides the chord arrows and the chord menu
1V/oct pitch for that note of the chord
Note — left-click or right-click the CHORD label to add, duplicate, cut, copy, paste or delete a chord; the arrows either side of it cycle through the list
Note — Rack's own preset menu carries a factory preset named All chords, which fills the list with 36 stored chords, from bare intervals through triads and sevenths to inversions
Menu — Sequencer direction — chooses what an ADV trigger does, from Forward, Reverse, Pendulum, Random and Brownian, which moves one chord up or down at random
Menu — Polyphonic outputs — makes output 2 carry notes 1 and 2, output 3 notes 1 to 3 and output 4 all four; output 1 is unchanged
Chords.notes: The two menu item names are literal strings in the binary, as are the five direction choices. The chord label's own menu carries New chord above, New chord below, Duplicate, Delete, Paste, Paste below and Transpose chord; it is not the module's right-click menu, which the note above says.
